discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect
subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases / mesoscopic transport)
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a new time-reversal-invariant electronic phase, the quantum spin Hall insulator. They characterised it by a Z2 topological invariant and protected helical edge states. Kane and co-workers then extended the idea to three-dimensional topological insulators and to proximity-induced topological superconductivity hosting Majorana modes. Molenkamp's group gave the decisive experimental test in 2007: quantised edge conductance near 2e^2/h, with nonlocal transport signatures, in HgTe quantum wells. Topological protection thus moved from mathematical concept to measured transport property. This work created a field. It reorganised band theory around topology, launched the worldwide search for topological materials, and underlies today's efforts toward topologically protected quantum devices. It is a rare case where elegant theory and experiment together established a genuinely new state of matter.
